record.title: The two-thirds minimum/maximum degree conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $k$ be a positive integer. **Two-thirds conjecture.** If $\delta(G)\ge\left\lfloor\frac{2k}{3}\right\rfloor$ and $\Delta(G)\ge k$, then $G$ contains every tree with $k$ edges. The conjecture seeks to replace the Erdős–Sós average-degree condition by simultaneous minimum- and maximum-degree conditions. The source records the spanning case and other partial results, but not a general resolution.
record.source_name: Maya Stein, “Tree containment and degree conditions”, arXiv:1912.04004 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.04004

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

record.title: Kummini–Lakshmibai–Sastry–Seshadri regularity conjecture for Grassmannian Schubert patches
record.statement:
Let $B\subseteq GL_n(\mathbb{C})$ be the Borel subgroup of upper triangular matrices, and let $w\in S_n$ be a Grassmannian permutation with descent at position $k$. Let $Y$ be the standard open patch associated with $w$, let $J_w$ be the prime ideal generated by the essential minors defining the corresponding patch $Y_w$, and suppose that for some $r\in[k-1]$ one has

$$
w_{k-r+i}=n-k+i\quad\text{for all }i\in[r]
$$

and $w_1=1$. Define $\widetilde w$ by $(\widetilde w_1,\ldots,\widetilde w_k)=(n-w_k+1,\ldots,n-w_1+1)$, write

$$
(\widetilde w_1,\ldots,\widetilde w_k)=(k-r+1,k-r+2,\ldots,k,a_{r+1},\ldots,a_{n-1},n),
$$

set $a_r=k$ and $a_k=n$, and, for $r\leq i\leq k-1$, define $m_i=a_{i+1}-a_i$. **Kummini–Lakshmibai–Sastry–Seshadri conjecture.** The regularity should satisfy

$$
\operatorname{reg}(\mathbb{C}[Y]/J_w)=\sum_{i=r}^{k-1}(m_i-1)i.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture is false and provides a counterexample, replacing it with an alternate explicit combinatorial formula for the regularity.
record.source_name: Jenna Rajchgot, Yi Ren, Colleen Robichaux, Avery St. Dizier and Anna Weigandt, “Degrees of symmetric Grothendieck polynomials and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity”, arXiv:1912.04477 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: Small-maximum-degree conjecture for tree versus wheel Ramsey numbers
record.statement:
Let $T_n$ be a tree on $n$ vertices, let $W_m$ be the wheel on $m+1$ vertices, and let $Delta(T_n)$ denote the maximum degree of $T_n$.

**Small-maximum-degree conjecture.** For even $m$ and $n>m\geq4$,

$$
\Delta(T_n)\leq n-m+2\quad\Rightarrow\quad R(T_n,W_m)=2n-1.
$$

This refines the earlier small-maximum-degree formulation by giving an explicit degree condition. It is presented as the paper’s refinement of the Chen–Zhang–Zhang conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

record.title: The 2n diagrams attain the upper bound on unknots
record.statement: A **free $2n$ knot** is the free knot diagram referred to in the source, with $n+2$ crossings. A minimal free knot diagram is one with the minimum crossing number for its knot. **$2n$-unknot upper-bound conjecture.** The free $2n$ knots realize the upper bound on unknots for minimal free knot diagrams with $n+2$ crossings. The source derives the resultant unknot probabilities for this family and uses them to motivate the proposed extremal bound; the conjecture itself is not proved in the supplied text.

record.title: Three-quarters exponent conjecture for acyclic subgraphs of tournaments
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be an $n$-vertex tournament. An **acyclic subgraph** is a subgraph with no directed cycle, and its chromatic number is the chromatic number of its underlying graph. **Three-quarters exponent conjecture.** The tournament $G$ has an acyclic subgraph with chromatic number at least

$$
n^{3/4-o(1)}.
$$

Equivalently, if $g(k)$ denotes the minimum integer such that every $g(k)$-vertex tournament has an acyclic subgraph with chromatic number $k$, then

$$
g(k)\le k^{4/3+o(1)}.
$$

The paper proves the bounds $k^{4/3-o(1)}\le g(k)\le k^{9/5+o(1)}$. The conjecture proposes that the lower-bound exponent is essentially sharp and remains open.
record.source_name: Jacob Fox, Matthew Kwan and Benny Sudakov, “Acyclic subgraphs of tournaments with high chromatic number”, arXiv:1912.07722 (2024).

record.title: Conjecture on the tabulated maximum values M(n,r_2)
record.statement: For each degree $n$ and signature parameter $r_2$, let $M(n,r_2)$ denote the maximum value of the corresponding function $Q(n,r_2,\{j_1,\ldots,j_{r_2}\},\cdot)$, with the conjectured upper bounds listed in Table. **Table-value conjecture.** The values in the table are the correct values. The conjecture records the numerical optimization results for the regulator-related functions $Q$; no proof or resolution is supplied in the source.

record.title: Erdős–Frankl–Pippenger classification conjecture for intersecting permutation families
record.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group on $[n]$. A family $\mathcal{F} \subset S_n$ is **$t$-intersecting** if every two permutations in $\mathcal{F}$ agree on at least $t$ points. For $0 \leq i \leq (n-t)/2$, define

$$
\mathcal{F}_i:= \{\sigma \in S_n: \sigma \text{ has at least } t+i \text{ fixed points in } [t+2i]\}.
$$

A **double translate** of a family is a family of the form $\pi\mathcal{F}_i\tau$ for $\pi,\tau \in S_n$. **Erdős–Frankl–Pippenger conjecture.** For any $n,t \in \mathbb{N}$, every maximum-sized $t$-intersecting family in $S_n$ is a double translate of one of the families $\mathcal{F}_i$.

This conjecture proposes a complete classification of extremal $t$-intersecting permutation families. The source explicitly says that it remains open.
record.source_name: David Ellis and Noam Lifshitz, “Approximation by juntas in the symmetric group, and forbidden intersection problems”, arXiv:1912.09228 (2019).

record.title: Clique-counting conjecture for bounded-degree graphs with a fixed number of edges
record.statement:
Let $t\geq 3$, let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges and maximum degree at most $r$, and write

$$
m=a\binom{r+1}{2}+b,\qquad 0\leq b<\binom{r+1}{2}.
$$

Here $k_t(G)$ denotes the number of copies of $K_t$ in $G$, $K_{r+1}$ is the complete graph on $r+1$ vertices, and $\mathcal{C}(b)$ is the colex graph with $b$ edges. **Bounded-degree edge-resource clique-counting conjecture.** One has

$$
k_t(G)\leq k_t\bigl(aK_{r+1}\cup\mathcal{C}(b)\bigr).
$$

The conjecture refines the paper's main theorem, which proves the analogous assertion for the total number of cliques. The source attributes this refinement to the authors' earlier work, but gives no resolution status, so it remains open here.

record.title: The regular Turán bound for 3-chromatic graphs built from bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a 3-chromatic graph obtained from a bipartite graph by adding a set of independent edges into one part. Write $\mathrm{rex}(n,F)$ for the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex, regular, $F$-free graph.

**Regular Turán bound.** For such a graph $F$,

$$
\mathrm{rex}(n,F)\le (1+o(1))\frac{n^2}{5}.
$$

This bound is presented in the source as an assertion for a class of 3-chromatic graphs in the study of regular Turán numbers. Because the statement appears as a standalone claim but is not identified there as a conjecture or accompanied by a resolution status, its status should be checked against the surrounding paper; it is recorded here as open.

record.title: Babai's motion conjecture for primitive distance-regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 3$, and let $X$ be a primitive distance-regular graph of diameter $d$ on $n$ vertices. Write $\operatorname{motion}(X)$ for the minimum number of vertices moved by a nonidentity automorphism of $X$.

**Babai's motion conjecture.** There exists an $\alpha>0$ such that either

$$
\operatorname{motion}(X)\geq \alpha n,
$$

or $X$ is a Hamming graph, or a Johnson graph.

This is the specialization of Babai's coherent-configuration conjecture to primitive distance-regular graphs. The paper discusses partial results, including the rank-$3$ and rank-$4$ cases, but the general statement remains open.

record.title: Counting conjecture for real critical points of cyclotomic polynomials
record.statement:
Let $n$ be an odd square-free integer with $k$ distinct prime factors, and let $N_n$ denote the number of real roots of $\Phi_n^{\prime}$. For primes $p$ not dividing $n$, write $N_{np}$ similarly. **Counting conjecture.**

$$
2k-1\leq N_n\leq 2^k-1.
$$

Moreover, $N_n=2k-1$ if $n$ is the product of the $k$ smallest odd primes, and if $p<p'$ are primes not dividing $n$, then $N_{np}\leq N_{np'}$. These bounds and monotonicity are suggested by computations and by the proof of the main result, but are presented as open challenges.
record.source_name: Hoon Hong and Andrew J. Sommese, “Number of Real Critical Points of Cyclotomic Polynomials”, arXiv:1912.12253 (2019).

record.title: Half finite approximation conjecture
record.statement:
Assume Hilbert spaces are separable with complex scalars. Let $\mathscr{X}$ be a Hilbert space, let $\rho:\mathbb{F}\times\mathbb{F}\to\mathrm{U}(\mathscr{X})$ be a unitary representation, let $x\in\mathscr{X}$ be a unit vector, let $E,F\subseteq\mathbb{F}$ be finite, and let $\epsilon>0$. A representation is **half finite** when it factors through a finite quotient in the first copy of $\mathbb{F}$ and the identity in the second copy. **Existence of half finite approximations.** There exist a Hilbert space $\mathscr{Y}$, a finite quotient $\Gamma$ of $\mathbb{F}$, a half finite unitary representation $\zeta:\mathbb{F}\times\mathbb{F}\to\Gamma\times\mathbb{F}\to\mathrm{U}(\mathscr{Y})$, and a unit vector $y\in\mathscr{Y}$ such that

$$
\left|\langle\rho(g,g')x,x\rangle-\langle\zeta(g,g')y,y\rangle\right|\leq\epsilon
$$

for all $g\in E$ and $g'\in F$. The paper states that this conjecture would imply Connes' embedding conjecture, but the supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: Peter Burton and Kate Juschenko, “Extension of positive definite functions and Connes' embedding conjecture”, arXiv:1912.12365 (2020).

record.title: Collapsibility bound for independence complexes of bounded-degree graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $I_n(G)$ denote its complex of independent sets of size at most $n$. For a simplicial complex $X$, let $C(X)$ denote its collapsibility number. Let $\Delta$ be a nonnegative integer and let $n$ be a positive integer.

**Collapsibility conjecture.** If $G$ has maximum degree at most $\Delta$, then

$$
C(I_n(G))\leq\left\lceil\frac{\Delta+1}{2}\right\rceil(n-1).
$$

This is proposed as an extension of the Aharoni–Briggs–Kim–Kim conjecture. The bound is known for claw-free graphs, but the paper gives counterexamples in general, so the conjecture is refuted.
record.source_name: Minki Kim and Alan Lew, “Complexes of graphs with bounded independence number”, arXiv:1912.12605 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.12605

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2019). “For the subclass of claw-free graphs, this is proved in Proposition .”

record.title: Link collapsibility conjecture for independence complexes of bounded-degree graphs
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, and let $I_n(G)$ be its independence complex. For an independent set $A$ of size $n-1$, let $\operatorname{lk}(I_n(G),A)$ denote the link of $A$ in $I_n(G)$. Let $C(X)$ denote the collapsibility number of a simplicial complex $X$, and let $n\geq 1$.

**Link collapsibility conjecture.** If $A$ is an independent set of size $n-1$ in $G$, then

$$
C(\operatorname{lk}(I_n(G),A))\leq\left\lfloor\frac{(n-1)\Delta}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This is presented as a weaker result that may hold for general bounded-degree graphs, after the stronger global collapsibility bound was disproved. Its status is open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Minki Kim and Alan Lew, “Complexes of graphs with bounded independence number”, arXiv:1912.12605 (2019).

record.title: The local weak limit conjecture for random intersection graphs
record.statement: Construct the locally finite connected rooted random graph $G^\bullet$ from the partially labeled rooted random tree $T^\bullet$ as described in the source: even-generation vertices have offspring distribution $\operatorname{Poi}(\lambda)$, odd-generation vertices carry independent $X$-biased labels $(X^*,Q^*)$ and have $X^*-1$ children, and edges between even-generation vertices are retained according to the independent Bernoulli variables attached to odd-generation layers. **Local weak limit conjecture.** Under sufficient regularity, $G^\bullet$ is a local weak limit of the random intersection graph model. This conjecture identifies the rooted tree construction as the local limit of the model; the source does not specify the regularity assumptions or give a resolution.

record.title: Constant-cycle subvariety vanishing conjecture for moduli spaces of sheaves on K3 surfaces
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a K3 surface and ${\mathsf M}$ a moduli space of stable sheaves on $X$ of dimension $2n$. Let $V\subset {\mathsf M}$ be a **constant-cycle subvariety**, meaning that all points of $V$ have the same class in $CH_0({\mathsf M})$. Let $\overline{\Delta}_{0j}$ denote the modified diagonal correspondence between the first ${\mathsf M}$ factor and the $j$th factor of ${\mathsf M}^{n+1}$. **Constant-cycle subvariety vanishing conjecture.** One has

$$
[V]\cdot\overline{\Delta}_{01}\cdot\overline{\Delta}_{02}\cdots\overline{\Delta}_{0,n+1}=0
$$

in $CH_{\star}({\mathsf M}\times {\mathsf M}^{n+1})$, where $[V]$ is pulled back from the first ${\mathsf M}$ factor. This generalizes the corresponding zero-cycle identity and seeks a uniform Chow-theoretic relation for constant-cycle subvarieties of all dimensions.

record.title: Ishii's bounded blow-up conjecture for minimal log discrepancies
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$. For a singularity $(X,x)$ of dimension $n$ embedded into a smooth variety $A$ with $\dim A=\mathrm{emb}(X,x)$, let $I_X$ be the defining ideal of $X$, set $c=\mathrm{emb}(X,x)-n$, and let $b(E)$ denote the minimum number of successive blow-ups along the centers of a prime divisor $E$ over $A$ needed for $E$ to appear. **Ishii's bounded blow-up conjecture.** There is an integer $B_n\in\mathbb N$, depending only on $n$, such that a prime divisor $E$ over $A$ computes $\mathrm{mld}(x;A,I_X^c)$ and satisfies

$$
b(E)\leq B_n.
$$
 Ishii posed this conjecture; the supplied text does not state a resolution, so its status remains open here.

record.title: The cop-number conjecture for graphs without long holes
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph without a hole of length at least $t$, where $t\geq 6$. A **cop** is one player in the cops-and-robber game on $G$, and the **cop number** is the minimum number of cops needed to capture the robber.

**Cop-number conjecture.** The graph $G$ can be won by $t-4$ cops.

The preceding argument gives the bound $t-3$ cops, so this conjecture proposes improving it by one. Its first case, that two cops suffice for graphs without holes of length at least six, is highlighted as particularly interesting; the source states that the conjecture remains open.

record.title: Huang–Zhao matching conjecture for minimum vertex degree
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a $k$-graph on $n$ vertices, let $\delta_1(H)$ denote its minimum vertex degree, and let $\nu(H)$ denote the maximum size of a matching in $H$.

**Huang–Zhao conjecture.** For positive integers $m,k,n$ satisfying $m<n/k$, if

$$
\delta_1(H)>\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-m}{k-1},
$$

then

$$
\nu(H)\geq m.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the cited theorem of Huang and Zhao by replacing the hypothesis $n\geq 3k^2m$ with the natural range $m<n/k$. It concerns sharp minimum vertex-degree conditions forcing a matching of prescribed size and remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Mingyang Guo, Hongliang Lu and Yaolin Jiang, “Improved Bound on Vertex Degree Version of Erdős Matching Conjecture”, arXiv:2001.02820 (2022).

record.title: Gawron's conjecture on the order of longest twins in permutations
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, and let $\pi$ be a permutation of $[n]$. Two similar disjoint sub-permutations of $\pi$ are called **twins**. Let $t(\pi)$ be the largest integer $k$ such that $\pi$ contains a pair of twins of length $k$, and let

$$
t(n)=\min\{t(\pi):\pi\text{ is a permutation of }[n]\}.
$$

**Gawron's conjecture.** We have

$$
t(n)=\Theta(n^{2/3}).
$$

The Erdős–Szekeres theorem gives the lower bound $t(n)=\Omega(\sqrt n)$, while Gawron's probabilistic argument gives $t(n)=O(n^{2/3})$. The conjecture asserts that the latter bound has the correct order of growth.
record.source_name: Andrzej Dudek, Jarosław Grytczuk and Andrzej Ruciński, “Variations on twins in permutations”, arXiv:2001.05589 (2020).

record.title: Sørensen's conjecture on Hermitian surface intersections
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $F\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}[x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3]$ be homogeneous of degree $d$, and let $V_2\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ be a non-degenerate Hermitian surface defined over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. For $d\leq q$, **Sørensen's conjecture.**

$$
\left|(V(F)\cap V_2)(\mathbb{F}_{q^2})\right|\leq d(q^3+q^2-q)+q+1.
$$

Moreover, equality holds precisely for surfaces defined by a homogeneous polynomial whose zero locus is a union of $d$ planes in $\mathbb{P}^3(\mathbb{F}_{q^2})$, each tangent to $V_2$, all containing a common line $\ell$ that intersects $V_2$ in $q+1$ points. The conjecture gives the maximal number of rational points in such intersections and determines the minimum distance of the associated codes; the paper's abstract states that it proves Sørensen's conjecture.
record.source_name: Peter Beelen, Mrinmoy Datta and Masaaki Homma, “A proof of Sørensen's conjecture on Hermitian surfaces”, arXiv:2001.07082 (2020).

record.title: Conjecture on the semiclassical ground-state limit for non-degenerate minima
record.statement: Let $M$ be a connected manifold and let $V$ be a potential whose minima are non-degenerate in the sense of Shubin's Condition C. Let $\lambda_t$ denote the relevant analytic eigenvalue branch in the semiclassical parameter $t$. **Semiclassical ground-state limit conjecture.** Then $t^{-2}\lambda_t$ converges to the absolute minimum of $V$. The claim extends the one-dimensional conclusion suggested by the simplicity and ordering of the spectrum; its general validity under the stated non-degeneracy and connectedness assumptions is left as a conjectural assertion.

record.title: Conjecture on the eternal game chromatic number of even random graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_{n,p}$ be the random graph on $n$ vertices in which each edge is present independently with probability $p$, where $n$ is even and $p$ is a fixed constant in $(0,1)\setminus\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{3},\dots\}$. Let $\chi_g^{\infty}(G)$ denote the smallest number of colours for which Alice has a winning strategy in the eternal vertex colouring game on $G$. **Eternal game chromatic number conjecture.** There exists $\epsilon>0$ such that, with high probability,

$$
\chi_g^{\infty}(G_{n,p}) \leq (1-\epsilon)\frac{pn}{2}.
$$

For even $n$, the known upper bound is $(1+o(1))pn/2$, and equality at this scale is known when $p=1/l$ for some $l\in\mathbb N$; the conjecture concerns the unresolved remaining values of $p$.
record.source_name: Vojtěch Dvořák, Rebekah Herrman and Peter van Hintum, “The Eternal Game Chromatic Number of Random Graphs”, arXiv:2001.08705 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08705

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2020). “For the unresolved case when $n$ is even and $p\not\in\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{3},\dots\}$, we conjecture the following.”

record.title: The hyperplane fraction conjecture for the symmetric-group orbit
record.statement:
Let $S_n$ act on $\mathbb{R}^n$ by permuting coordinates. For $n\geq 3$, let $v$ range over vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with distinct coordinates and not lying in the hyperplane

$$
\sum_i x_i=0.
$$

Let $H\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ range over hyperplanes through the origin. **Hyperplane fraction conjecture.** Then

$$
\max_{v,H} \lvert H\cap S_nv\rvert=\begin{cases}(n-1)!,& n\text{ is odd},\
(n-2)!,& n\text{ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture gives the exact maximum fraction of a free $S_n$-orbit that can lie in a hyperplane through the origin. The paper proves an upper bound using the largest prime $p\leq n$, and in particular establishes the conjecture when $n$ or $n-1$ is prime; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Jiahui Huang, David McKinnon and Matthew Satriano, “What fraction of an S_n-orbit can lie on a hyperplane?”, arXiv:2001.09123 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.09123

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).

record.title: Hasse-diagram chromatic number gap conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a Hasse diagram on $n$ vertices, and let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number. **Hasse-diagram chromatic number gap conjecture.** There exists $\epsilon>0$ such that

$$
\chi(G)\leq n^{1/2-\epsilon}.
$$

The paper proves a lower bound of order $\Omega(n^{1/4})$ for the largest possible chromatic number of a Hasse diagram, while the general upper bound for triangle-free graphs is $n^{1/2+o(1)}$. Whether a power gap below $n^{1/2}$ always holds remains open.
record.source_name: Andrew Suk and István Tomon, “Hasse diagrams with large chromatic number”, arXiv:2001.09901 (2020).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.09901

record.title: Xu's conditional edge-connectivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k,h$ be integers, and let $G$ be a connected graph with minimum degree at least $k$. Let $a_h(G)$ be the minimum cardinality of a vertex set of an $h$-regular subgraph of $G$. If $\boldsymbol{\lambda^h(G)}$ exists, then

**Xu's conjecture.**

$$
\lambda^h(G) \leq a_h(G)(k-h).
$$

This conjecture concerns the conditional edge-connectivity of graphs and is stated here in connection with multidimensional tori and $k$-ary $r$-cubes. The supplied material does not establish its general status beyond the paper's result for those graph classes.
record.source_name: J. B. Saraf, Y. M. Borse and Ganesh Mundhe, “On conditional connectivity of the Cartesian product of cycles”, arXiv:2001.11781 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.11781

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).

record.title: Dunbar-Haynes-Teschner-Volkmann planar bondage-number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $Delta(G)$ denote its maximum vertex degree and $b(G)$ its bondage number, the smallest number of edges whose removal increases the domination number. **Dunbar-Haynes-Teschner-Volkmann conjecture.** If $G$ is a planar graph then we have

$$
b(G)\leq \Delta(G)+1.
$$

This is one of two stated upper-bound conjectures for the bondage number, and the source identifies these conjectures as still open.
record.source_name: Jia Huang and Jian Shen, “New upper bounds for the bondage number of a graph in terms of its maximum degree and Euler characteristic”, arXiv:2002.00765 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1111.5629](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.5629).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.00765

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2020). “There are two conjectures on upper bounds of $b(G)$, which are still open.”

record.title: Maximum monotone paths conjecture for simple 3-dimensional polytopes
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a simple $3$-dimensional polytope with $2n$ vertices, and let $f$ be a generic linear functional on $P$. Let $\b5(P,f)$ denote the number of $f$-monotone paths on $P$, and let $(F_n)$ be the Fibonacci sequence defined by $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_n=F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}$ for $n\geq 2$. **Maximum monotone paths conjecture.** We have

$$
\mu(P,f)\leq F_{n+2}+1.
$$

The proposed maximum can be achieved by wedges of polygons over an edge whose vertices are the source and the sink, with all vertices of the polytope lying on a monotone path; the claim concerns the expected extremal number among simple $3$-dimensional polytopes.
record.source_name: Christos Athanasiadis, Jesús De Loera and Zhenyang Zhang, “Enumerative problems for arborescences and monotone paths on polytope graphs”, arXiv:2002.00999 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.00999

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: The total Roman domination function support conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\gamma_{tR}(G)$ denote its total Roman domination number, and let $V_f^+$ be the set of vertices assigned a positive value by a $\gamma_{tR}(G)$-function $f$. A graph is **$\gamma_{tR}$-edge-supercritical** if every missing edge is supercritical with respect to total Roman domination.

**Support conjecture.** If $G$ is a $\gamma_{tR}$-edge-supercritical graph and $v\in V(G)$, then there exists a $\gamma_{tR}(G)$-function $f$ such that $v\in V_f^+$.

This conjecture would provide a positive-valued vertex in a minimum total Roman dominating function at every vertex of an edge-supercritical graph. The source presents it as the first of two conjectures, with the second described as a direct consequence of this one; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: C. M. Mynhardt and S. E. A. Ogden, “Total Roman Domination Edge-Supercritical and Edge-Removal-Supercritical Graphs”, arXiv:2002.01347 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01347

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: Extremal-graph classification conjecture for triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $n$ and $s$ be integers with $n/3<s\le n/2$, and let $\mathrm{ex}(n,s)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with independence number at most $s$. Let $g_k(n,s)$ be the functions defined in the preceding conjecture, and let $\mathscr{G}^n_k(s)$ and $\mathscr{H}^n_k(s)$ be the graph families described in the source. **Extremal-graph classification conjecture.** If $G$ has $\mathrm{ex}(n,s)$ edges, then $G$ is isomorphic to a graph in one of the families $\mathscr{G}^n_k(s)$ or $\mathscr{H}^n_k(s)$, and

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,s)=\min_k g_k(n,s).
$$

The source proves the classification in a neighbourhood to the right of each critical ratio, but strongly suspects that it holds throughout the full range.
record.source_name: Tomasz Łuczak, Joanna Polcyn and Christian Reiher, “Andrásfai and Vega graphs in Ramsey-Turán theory”, arXiv:2002.01498 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01498

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2020). “This was refuted by H\"aggkvist , who found a $10$-regular triangle-free graph on $29$ vertices whose chromatic number is four.”

record.title: The sharp upper-bound conjecture for the Yokota invariant
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a planar $3$-connected graph, let $\overline{\Gamma}$ denote the associated maximal-volume proper generalized hyperbolic polyhedron, and let $col$ be any $r$-admissible coloring of the edges of $\Gamma$. **The sharp upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
\frac{\pi}{r}\log\left\lvert Y_r(\Gamma,col)\right\rvert\leq \operatorname{Vol}(\overline{\Gamma})+O\left(\frac{\log(r)}{r}\right).
$$

Moreover, the inequality is sharp, with equality attained by the sequence of colorings assigning $\frac{r-2\pm1}{2}$ to every edge, with the sign chosen so that the colors are even. This is presented as a sharper conjecture following the maximum volume conjecture. Its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Giulio Belletti, “An upper bound conjecture for the Yokota invariant”, arXiv:2002.01904 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01904

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: The mixed-volume Minkowski-sum volume conjecture
record.statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer, let $m$ be a real number, and let $K_1,\ldots,K_d$ be convex bodies in $\mathds{R}^d$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{Vol}(K_1) \ge 1,\ \ldots,\ \operatorname{Vol}(K_d) \ge 1,\quad\text{and }\ \operatorname{V}(K_1,\ldots,K_d)=m.
$$

For an integer $\ell$ with $1\leq\ell\leq d$, **the mixed-volume Minkowski-sum volume conjecture.** The maximum of $\operatorname{Vol}(K_1+\cdots+K_\ell)$ equals $(m+\ell-1)^d$ and is attained when $K_1=mK_2=\cdots=mK_d$ with $\operatorname{Vol}(K_d)=1$.
record.source_name: Gennadiy Averkov, Christopher Borger and Ivan Soprunov, “Inequalities between mixed volumes of convex bodies: volume bounds for the Minkowski sum”, arXiv:2002.03065 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.03065

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: Lewis–Reiner's Hurwitz orbit conjecture for reflection factorizations
record.statement: Let $W$ be a well-generated finite complex reflection group, and let $T$ and $T'$ be reflection factorizations of a Coxeter element of $W$. Two factorizations are said to have the same **multiset of conjugacy classes** when the multisets formed by the conjugacy classes of their reflection factors coincide. **Lewis–Reiner's conjecture.** $T$ and $T'$ lie in the same Hurwitz orbit if and only if they share the same multiset of conjugacy classes. The conjecture predicts that these conjugacy-class data completely determine Hurwitz orbits of reflection factorizations of Coxeter elements; the paper confirms it for the complex reflection group $G_6$.
record.source_name: Gaurav Gawankar, Dounia Lazreq, Mehr Rai and Seth Sabar, “Hurwitz Actions on Reflection Factorizations in Complex Reflection Group G_6”, arXiv:2002.05102 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1808.01268](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.01268).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05102

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Tree-chromatic weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $t$ be an integer. The **tree-chromatic number** $\mathsf{tree}\textnormal{-}\chi(G)$ is the minimum, over tree-decompositions of $G$, of the maximum chromatic number of a bag. **Tree-chromatic Hadwiger conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph without a $K_{t+1}$-minor, then $\mathsf{tree}\textnormal{-}\chi(G) \leqslant t$. This is proposed as a weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture and is open; the paper proves it for $t=5$ without using the Four Colour Theorem.
record.source_name: Tony Huynh, Bruce Reed, David R. Wood and Liana Yepremyan, “Notes on Tree- and Path-chromatic Number”, arXiv:2002.05363 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05363

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: Samuels' conjecture on sums of independent non-negative random variables
record.statement:
Let $0\leq c_1\leq\cdots\leq c_l$ with $\sum_{i=1}^l c_i<1$. Consider $l$ independent non-negative random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_l$ satisfying $\mathbf E[X_i]=c_i$. Let $k$ be an integer, let $\beta_j$ be Bernoulli random variables for $j>k$, and set

$$
b=\sum_{i=1}^k c_i.
$$

**Samuels' conjecture.** The supremum of $\mathbf P(X_1+\cdots+X_l\geq1)$ over all such collections is a maximum attained by $X_j=c_j$ for $j\leq k$ and $X_j=(1-b)\beta_j$ for $j>k$.

The conjecture predicts that an optimizer accumulates the smaller expectations deterministically before switching to bold play. The source presents it as an open conjecture and notes that, when all expectations are equal, it predicts optimization by a binomial.
record.source_name: Robbert Fokkink, Ludolf Meester and Christos Pelekis, “Optimizing stakes in simultaneous bets”, arXiv:2002.06804 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1602.03547](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03547).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06804

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2020). “The following has been conjectured by Cs\'oka , who was inspired by some well known open problems in combinatorics:”

record.title: The asymptotic degree of the bubble-sort map on partitions
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Part}(n)$ denote the set of partitions of $n$, and let $\mathscr B:\operatorname{Part}(n)\to\operatorname{Part}(n)$ be the bubble-sort map. Write $\deg(\mathscr B:\operatorname{Part}(n)\to\operatorname{Part}(n))$ for its maximum fiber size.

**Bubble-sort degree conjecture.**

$$
\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\deg(\mathscr B:\operatorname{Part}(n)\to\operatorname{Part}(n))=3.
$$

Computations for random partitions suggest that the degrees are close to $3$, but the paper states that no method is currently known to improve the preceding estimates.
record.source_name: Colin Defant and James Propp, “Quantifying Noninvertibility in Discrete Dynamical Systems”, arXiv:2002.07144 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.07144

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: Kalai's tight-tree conjecture for tight paths
record.statement:
For $n \geq r \geq 2$ and $k \geq 1$, let $P_k^r$ be the tight $k$-path in an $r$-uniform hypergraph, and let ${\rm ex}(n,P_k^r)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no tight $k$-path. **Kalai's conjecture.**

$$
{\rm ex}(n,P_k^r) \leq \frac{k-1}{r}{n \choose r-1}.
$$

This is presented as a special case of Kalai's conjecture on tight trees, generalizing the Erdős–Sós conjecture. The claim concerns the extremal number of tight paths in uniform hypergraphs; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Zoltán Füredi, Tao Jiang, Alexandr Kostochka, Dhruv Mubayi and Jacques Verstraëte, “Tight paths in convex geometric hypergraphs”, arXiv:2002.09457 (2020).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1912.11421](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.11421), [arXiv:1912.04004](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.04004), [arXiv:1711.07442](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.07442).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.09457

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: Vizing-Goldberg type gap-one conjecture for equitable coloring of block graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a block graph. Write $\omega(G)$ for its clique number, $\alpha_{\min}(G)$ for the minimum size of a maximal independent set, and $\chi_{=}(G)$ for its equitable chromatic number. **Gap-one conjecture.**

$$
\max \left\\{\omega(G),\left\lceil \frac{|V(G)|+1}{\alpha_{\min}(G)+1}\right\rceil\right\\} \leq \chi_{=}(G) \leq 1+\max \left\\{\omega(G),\left\lceil \frac{|V(G)|+1}{\alpha_{\min}(G)+1}\right\rceil\right\\}.
$$

The lower bound follows from general constraints on equitable colorings, while the conjecture asserts that the upper bound is at most one larger. The paper confirms the conjecture for well-covered block graphs, those satisfying $\alpha_{\min}(G)=\alpha(G)$; the general case is left open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Janusz Dybizbański, Hanna Furmańczyk and Vahan Mkrtchyan, “Vizing-Goldberg type bounds for the equitable chromatic number of block graphs”, arXiv:2002.10151 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10151

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: Transience conjecture for the frog model on supercritical Galton–Watson trees
record.statement:
Let $\mathsf{GW}$ be a Galton–Watson measure defined by $(p_i)_{i\geq 0}$ with mean offspring

$$
\sum_i i p_i>1.
$$

For a tree $\mathsf{T}$ sampled from $\mathsf{GW}$, let $\mathrm{FM}(\mathsf{T},\eta,\mathsf{SRW})$ denote the frog model with sleeping-frog mean $\bar{\eta}$.

**Transience conjecture.** There exists a constant $c=c(\mathsf{GW})>0$ such that $\mathrm{FM}(\mathsf{T},\eta,\mathsf{SRW})$ is transient for $\mathsf{GW}$-almost all infinite realizations $\mathsf{T}$ whenever $\bar{\eta}<c$.

The conjecture would extend the paper’s transient-phase result from offspring distributions with bounded support and sufficiently large minimum positive offspring to every supercritical Galton–Watson measure. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Sebastian Müller and Gundelinde Maria Wiegel, “On transience of frogs on Galton-Watson trees”, arXiv:2002.12008 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.12008

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: Adjoint Reidemeister torsion vanishing conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented compact $3$-manifold with torus boundary, and let $X^\mathrm{irr}(M)$ be the character variety of irreducible $\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$-representations. Suppose that every component of $X^\mathrm{irr}(M)$ has dimension $1$ and that the interior of $M$ admits a hyperbolic structure. For a boundary curve $\gamma\subset\partial M$, let $\mathbb{T}_{\gamma}$ denote the adjoint Reidemeister torsion and let

$$
\mathrm{tr}_{\gamma}:X^\mathrm{irr}(M)\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}
$$

be the trace function of $\gamma$. **Adjoint Reidemeister torsion vanishing conjecture.** For any boundary curve $\gamma\subset\partial M$ and generic $C\in\mathbb{C}$,

$$
\sum_{\chi_\rho\in\mathrm{tr}_{\gamma}^{-1}(C)}\frac{1}{\mathbb{T}_{\gamma}(\chi_\rho)}=0.
$$

The paper's abstract states that this conjectural identity is proved for all hyperbolic twist-knot exteriors, while the general claim under the stated hypotheses is presented as conjectural.
record.source_name: Seokbeom Yoon, “A vanishing identity on adjoint Reidemeister torsions of twist knots”, arXiv:2002.12576 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1911.10718](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10718).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.12576

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).
